statement.description: Deliver ordered packages within d days. Each day takes a consecutive prefix of the remaining packages, with total weight at most capacity. Find the smallest capacity allowing delivery of all packages.
statement.inputFormat: n and d, followed by n positive weights.
statement.outputFormat: Print the minimum capacity.
statement.approach: Binary search capacity between the heaviest package and total weight. A greedy scan computes days needed for a candidate capacity; feasibility is monotonic.
statement.complexity: O(n log(sum(weights))) time, O(n) input space.
hints: The capacity cannot be below the heaviest package.
A feasible capacity stays feasible when increased.

statement.description: Merge overlapping closed reservation intervals. Intervals that touch at an endpoint also merge.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n lines with start and end.
statement.outputFormat: Print the number of merged intervals, then each merged interval in increasing start order.
statement.approach: Sort intervals by start. Extend the current merged interval while the next start is at most the current end; otherwise begin a new interval.
statement.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
hints: Sorting brings potential overlaps together.
Touching closed endpoints count as overlap.

statement.description: Choose the largest number of meetings that fit in one room. A meeting may start exactly when the previous meeting ends.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n lines containing start and end.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum meeting count.
statement.approach: Sort by finishing time, then repeatedly take the earliest-finishing meeting compatible with the last chosen meeting.
statement.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) storage.
hints: Choosing the longest or earliest-starting meeting can block better choices.
The earliest finish leaves the most time for later meetings.

statement.description: Start at index 0. At index i you may jump forward between 1 and a[i] positions. Decide whether the last index is reachable; a one-element array is already at the exit.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n maximum jump lengths.
statement.outputFormat: Print YES or NO.

statement.description: A staircase has n steps. Each move climbs one or two steps. Count the distinct move sequences that reach the top, modulo 1000000007. For zero steps, the empty sequence counts once.
statement.inputFormat: One integer n.
statement.outputFormat: Print the number of routes modulo 1000000007.

hints: The base cases are ways(0)=1 and ways(1)=1.

statement.description: You have unlimited tokens of each listed positive denomination. Find the fewest tokens needed to pay an exact amount.
statement.inputFormat: n and amount, followed by n denominations.
statement.outputFormat: Print the minimum token count, or -1 when exact payment is impossible.
statement.approach: Let dp[x] be the minimum count for amount x. Start with dp[0]=0 and try each denomination as the final token.
hints: Always taking the biggest token is not generally optimal.
Unreachable amounts need a sentinel larger than any valid answer.

statement.description: Pick rewards from a line of stations without choosing adjacent stations. Find the maximum total reward; choosing no station is allowed.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n nonnegative rewards.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum obtainable reward.
statement.approach: For each station, either skip it and retain the previous optimum, or take it and add its reward to the optimum two positions back.
hints: Only the previous two optimal totals matter.
Taking the largest individual value is not enough.

statement.description: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Chosen elements preserve their original order but need not be adjacent.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n integers.
statement.outputFormat: Print the maximum subsequence length.

statement.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
hints: Equal values cannot extend a strictly increasing sequence.
Binary search the current tails array.

statement.description: Move from the top-left cell to the bottom-right using only right and down moves. A dot is open and # is blocked. Count valid routes modulo 1000000007.

statement.description: Count islands on a map of 0 (water) and 1 (land). Land cells connect only horizontally or vertically; diagonals do not connect.
statement.inputFormat: r and c, followed by r binary strings of length c.
statement.outputFormat: Print the island count.
statement.approach: Start an iterative flood fill at each unvisited land cell and mark its entire connected component. Each new flood fill contributes one island.
hints: Diagonal contacts are separate islands.
An iterative queue avoids recursion-depth problems on a large island.

statement.description: Find the fewest edges needed to travel from s to t in an undirected unweighted graph. Parallel edges are allowed.
statement.inputFormat: n, m, s and t, followed by m lines containing endpoints u and v. Nodes are numbered 0 to n−1.
statement.outputFormat: Print the shortest distance, or -1 if t is unreachable.
statement.approach: Breadth-first search discovers nodes in nondecreasing distance from the source. Assign each node a distance only on its first visit.
hints: Every edge has equal weight.
Mark a node when adding it to the queue.

statement.description: Each directed edge u→v means task u must finish before task v. Determine whether all tasks can be completed. Duplicate prerequisite edges are allowed.
statement.inputFormat: n and m, followed by m directed edges u v.
statement.outputFormat: Print YES if all tasks can be completed, otherwise NO.
statement.approach: Kahn’s algorithm repeatedly removes zero-indegree tasks. If fewer than n tasks are removed, a directed cycle remains.
hints: A directed cycle makes completion impossible.
Queue tasks that currently have no unmet prerequisites.

from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop

def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();m=ni();a=[[] for _ in range(n)];deg=[0]*n
for _ in range(m):u=ni();v=ni();a[u].append(v);deg[v]+=1
q=deque(i for i in range(n) if deg[i]==0);count=0
while q:
 u=q.popleft();count+=1
 for v in a[u]:
  deg[v]-=1
  if deg[v]==0:q.append(v)

statement.description: Connect all labs using some of the offered undirected cables at minimum total cost. If the offered cables cannot connect all labs, report failure. Parallel cables are allowed.
statement.inputFormat: n and m, followed by m lines containing u, v and cost.
statement.outputFormat: Print the minimum total cost, or -1 if impossible. One lab requires cost 0.
statement.approach: Kruskal’s algorithm sorts edges by cost and accepts an edge only when it joins different disjoint-set components. A spanning tree needs n−1 accepted edges.
statement.complexity: O(m log m) time, O(n+m) space.
hints: Taking a cable inside an already connected component creates an unnecessary cycle.
Use path compression and union by size.

from collections import deque, Counter
from bisect import bisect_left
from heapq import heappush, heappop
data = iter(sys.stdin.read().split())
def ni(): return int(next(data))
n=ni();m=ni();edges=[]
for _ in range(m):u=ni();v=ni();w=ni();edges.append((w,u,v))
edges.sort();p=list(range(n));sz=[1]*n
def root(x):
 while x!=p[x]:p[x]=p[p[x]];x=p[x]
 return x
cost=used=0
for w,u,v in edges:
 u=root(u);v=root(v)
 if u==v:continue
 if sz[u]<sz[v]:u,v=v,u
 p[v]=u;sz[u]+=sz[v];cost+=w;used+=1
print(cost if used==n-1 else -1)

statement.description: A binary tree is stored in array positions: root 0, left child 2i+1, right child 2i+2. A -1 marks a missing node. Print the sum of node values at each occupied depth. A completely empty tree prints EMPTY.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n array entries. Every present non-root node has a present parent.
statement.outputFormat: Print the sums from root depth downward, separated by spaces, or EMPTY.
constraints: Each entry is -1 or between 0 and 10^9.
statement.approach: Traverse present nodes using a queue. Process one queue-sized group per depth, summing its values and queuing existing children.
hints: Missing nodes contribute neither values nor children.
Snapshot the queue size to separate levels.

statement.description: A connected undirected tree contains n nodes. Find the number of edges in its longest simple path.
statement.inputFormat: n, followed by n−1 undirected edges u v. Nodes are numbered 0 to n−1.
statement.outputFormat: Print the tree diameter in edges.
constraints: The input is a valid tree.
statement.approach: BFS from any node finds an endpoint of a diameter. BFS again from that endpoint; its maximum distance is the diameter.
hints: The longest path need not go through node 0.
Use two breadth-first searches to avoid deep recursion.

statement.description: A monitor displays the largest value in every contiguous window of exactly k readings. Compute these peaks in left-to-right window order.
statement.inputFormat: n and k, followed by n integers.
statement.outputFormat: Print n−k+1 window maxima.
statement.approach: Keep candidate indices in a deque with decreasing values. Remove expired indices from the front and dominated values from the back. The front is the current maximum.
statement.complexity: O(n) time, O(k) auxiliary space beyond input/output.
hints: Recomputing each maximum costs O(nk).
The deque should store indices so expired values can be removed.
